Possibly from {{der|en|ine-pro|*bud-|t=to shoot, sprout}}, which would make it cognate with {{cog|sa|बुन्द||tr=bundá|arrow}}, {{cog|lt|budė}}, and {{m|lt|budis|t=mushroom, fungus}}. Compare also related {{cog|ang|pȳtan|t=to push, poke, thrust, put out (the eyes)}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|poten|t=to set, plant}}, {{cog|nds|paten|t=to set, plant}}, {{cog|da|putte|t=to put}}, {{cog|sv|putta}}, {{m|sv|pötta}}, {{m|sv|potta|t=to strike, knock, push gently, shove, put away}}, {{cog|no|putte|t=to set, put}}, {{cog|no|pota|t=to poke}}, {{cog|is|pota|t=to poke}}, {{cog|nl|peuteren|t=to pick, poke around, dig, fiddle with}}.

=====Usage notes=====
The verb "put" is unusual in that most senses require an adverbial for completion of the idea. For example, you cannot just "put a book", you must "put a book on the table", "put a book in the wastebin", etc.
